newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower on soybean sell-off.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower on soybean sell-off.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended a volatile day lower as a late profit-taking rally in soybeans wiped out earlier gains, traders said.

Soy products had traded quietly mixed most of the session but July soybean futures punctured strong resistance to move to new contract highs after noon, touching off buy stops and triggering sharp gains in soymeal and soyoil, traders said.
The new high for July soybeans is $8.95 per bushel, topping the previous high of $8.92-3/4 set on April 3.
But soybeans collapsed late on broad-based profit taking, prompting aggressive selling in other pits.
Soymeal futures were supported by tightening supplies as well as better-than-expected export sales, traders said.
Processors were said to be actively buying cash soymeal to cover trades for crushing plants that are taking downtime during the first half of May, meal traders said.
USDA put weekly net soymeal sales at 90,200 tonnes, above trade expectations for 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes. In contrast, weekly soyoil export sales were a disappointing 14,600 tonnes.
Soymeal ended $2.90 to $0.10 per ton lower with July down $2.90 at $283.90. Soyoil closed 0.30 to 0.15 cent per lb lower with July down 0.20 at 25.27.

On the day, funds sold at least 1,500 lots each soymeal and soyoil. Goldenberg-Hehmeyer sold 500 July soymeal, Prudential Securities and Smith Barney each sold 300 July and Dean Witter sold 200 July, pit sources said.
In sooyoil, Rosenthal Collins sold 600 July and Smith Barney sold 500 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 28,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's volume of 32,491 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 20,000 lots, against Wednesday's 26,800 lots.
